newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: RESEARCH ALERT - Goldman says buy FELS.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Goldman says buy FELS.

text.p: Goldman Sachs reiterated its buy recommendation on Far East Levingston Shipbuilding Ltd (FELS) on Tuesday despite the group's recent uninspiring interim results which showed a nine percent earnings decline.
"The 1996 results are of little consequence as the figures reflect market conditions two years ago," Goldman Sachs said in a research note on the oil rig repair and building company.
The big picture for rig building continues to improve even as competition heated up, it said.
"Offshore rig utilisation rates have hit 91.3 percent, and effective utilisation, which is now at 98 percent, should move higher over the next six to 12 months," it said.

Goldman Sachs said it expected strong demand growth for deepwater drilling equipment over the next five years due to improvements in technology resulting in cost reductions which have made marginal fields viable.

Goldman said FELS was expected to meet stiff competition from South Korean yards on rig building contracts. "However, we take comfort in the fact that FELS, with its solid track record and reputation, has exclusive agreements with several oil contractors such as Reading & Bates and Santa Fe."

It said it had raised the 1997 earnings per share forecast to Singapore $0.32 from S$0.30 while 1998 estimates had been lowered to S$0.47 from S$0.53 with one contract completion being pushed to 1999.

Goldman said it saw limited downside for FELS' share price and it should be supported by a net book value of S$5.18 a share. It said it expected major contract announcements to drive share price higher. -- Singapore Newsroom 65-8703080
